newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Saudi-Egyptian firm to start oil drilling in Saudi.
newsitem.headline: Saudi-Egyptian firm to start oil drilling in Saudi.

text.p: Saudi Arabian state oil firm Saudi Aramco said on Monday a joint Saudi-Egyptian firm would start drilling for oil in the kingdom in May.
"The Drilling and Petroleum Services Company (DPSC) rigs are scheduled to begin operations in the Ghawar field in mid-May 1997," a Saudi Aramco official said in a statement sent to Reuters.
"The two rigs under contract with DPSC will join a fleet of 36 rigs either owned by Saudi Aramco or under similar contracts with other firms to perform drilling services for Saudi Aramco," he added.
DPSC is owned by the Egyptian Drilling Company and Suwiket Trading Company of Saudi Arabia, the official said, but gave no details.

The official said oil exploration and field development activities in all company operating areas were performed exclusively by Saudi Aramco, using independent contractors where needed for specific drilling services.
He said that Saudi Aramco in mid-1996 contracted four additional rigs from two firms, including two rigs from DPSC.
"These contracts are limited to specific-area drilling services only, with Saudi Aramco supervising all operations," he said.
He did not name the second firm.
